messages:
Marco (AE): Heads-up 3 — customer's POC hit malformed JSON from function_call and a bunch of 429s during a live run. Need fast mitigation for tomorrow's exec demo.
Priya (Solutions): Customer summary: "using function_call + json_mode=legacy_strict, some responses arrive with trailing commas or cut mid-object. Also seeing 429 with X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0 when they ramp to ~30 parallel sims."
Kofi (Runtime): Can you paste one sanitized request/response and include x-request-id and model+streaming flag? Also how many tokens per response?
Marco (AE): Sanitzed clip from customer harness (they removed PII):
```
POST /v1/generate
{"model":"redwood-large-v2","json_mode":"legacy_strict","function_call":{"name":"settle_batch"},"max_tokens":1600}
HEADERS: x-request-id: demo-517, x-api-key: redacted

RESP 200 body: "{\"batch_id\":\"b-77\",\"status\":\"ok\",\"processed\":42, }"  <-- trailing comma then EOF

Later RESP 429 HEADERS: x-request-id: demo-518, x-rate-limit-remaining: 0, x-rate-limit-policy: burst
```
Dana (Oncall): Two separate problems: (1) serializer/chunking causing truncated output; (2) burst throttle. Short term: lower concurrency, add jittered exponential backoff.
Priya (Solutions): Quick mitigation suggestions for the customer: switch json_mode to "permissive"/"lax" for demo, reduce max_tokens (or paginate responses), or enable streaming and assemble client-side. If they must demo at 30 concurrent, ask for a temporary QPS bump.
Kofi (Runtime): I can enable a per-key tolerant parser that auto-closes braces and allows trailing commas for a 6-hour demo window, with full audit logs. Security needs to sign off. Also we can temporarily raise per-key QPS from 30->60 for 2 hours if approved.
Security Bot: Automated check: "tolerant-parser" raises parsing risk and could mask data issues. Approval required: demo-only key, TTL <= 6h, and explicit audit log retention.
Dana (Oncall): If they reproduce, get me the exact x-request-id(s) and UTC window and I'll pull edge + kernel traces. I can also attach a temporary ingress rule to increase burst capacity once Security ok.
Priya (Solutions): They're also asking for Dedicated/Private cost comparison (KMS + VPC + audit logs). Marco, I'll draft a quick numbers email once we know the expected tokens/sec and cache hit rate.
Marco (AE): Ask to reduce concurrency to <=10 and enable jittered backoff for now. I'll request Security approval for tolerant-parser and QPS bump.
Kofi (Runtime): Long-term advice to customer: 1) prefer streaming=true + client-side assembly (we'll share a robust reassembly helper), 2) use structured function response with an explicit "payload_base64" field if payloads are binary-ish, 3) add client-side size checks and retry with backoff.
Priya (Solutions): I'll attach a short Node snippet for streaming reassembly and a suggested retry policy: base backoff 200ms, factor 2, jitter 30%, max attempts 6.
Marco (AE): Action items: 1) Customer to drop concurrency and attempt repro + paste failing x-request-id. 2) Kofi/Dana prepare tolerant-parser + QPS bump plan pending Security. 3) Priya to draft Dedicated/Private cost sketch for exec stakeholders. 4) Marco to collect security questionnaire items from customer and forward.
Dana (Oncall): Noted incident id inc-2026-03-21-205. I'll attach traces when we have x-request-id.
Marco (AE): Thanks team 44d I'll post the x-request-id when the customer reproduces.
Priya (Solutions): cc @Kofi and @Dana for the quick patch plan.
Kofi (Runtime): I'll prep the tolerant-parser toggle and a terse rollback plan (flip off flag + revoke demo key) so Security has mitigation ready.
Security Bot: Reminder: include audit link and TTL in approval request.
